plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and increase cash.
Add to QQQI to increase income exposure.

conservative.read: This mode aims for low, steady gains around 1.5% per month. The focus is on preserving capital by cutting leverage and reducing concentration, leading to lower potential drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to small positions.
Reduce SPY to 25% to meet concentration mandate.
Initiate a small position in SOXS as a hedge.
Trim QQQI to rebalance the portfolio.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This mode targets approximately 2.5% monthly growth by balancing risk reduction and growth. It trims leverage and concentration while adding a hedge, aiming for moderate drawdowns.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each.
Add a 6% position in SOXS for hedging.
Increase CRWD to 20% to concentrate on a strong performer.
Add a new 10% position in META.
This aggressive plan aims for high growth but carries significant risk.
aggressive.read: This mode targets around 4% monthly growth by leaning into leverage and concentration. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring tech names. Expect higher potential upside and substantially larger drawdowns, with leverage decay being a key risk.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to increase cash holdings.
Significantly increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
Sell CRWD and SMH to eliminate high-beta and sector concentration.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and capital preservation.
income.read: This mode targets around 1% monthly growth, focusing on reliable income distributions. It cuts leverage and high-beta names, maximizing exposure to income-generating assets like QQQI. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
